Hi Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — great discussion on the document summarization and triage use case. Per our chat, I wanted to capture an actionable onramp so your engineering and ML teams can start a focused comparison on Redwood. TL;DR: we recommend starting with a small, representative scoring set (2–4k examples), running two model variants (rwd-13b-v1-q4 and rwd-7b-v2) on our hosted dev cluster, and using the attached schema + prompt set.

Action items assigned to MercuryAI:
- Share a representative CSV (see attached sample schema): id, source_type, raw_text, expected_label(s), sensitivity_flag (yes/no), notes. 
- Mark any PII/sensitivity examples; we can run a masked test if preferred.

What Redwood will provide for this eval:
- A hosted evaluation run: isolated dev queue, stable seed, token-level cost breakdown.
- Two recommended model variants to start: rwd-13b-v1 (quantized, cost-focused) and rwd-7b-v2 (latency-optimized).
- Scoring rubric and an initial prompt set (attached) plus a scoring script we can run against your ground truth.
- A short regression check against your control prompts to flag any quality drift.

Attachments sent with this message: mercuryai-benchmark-schema.csv (CSV schema + example rows), sample-prompt-set.md, redwood-eval-quickstart.pdf (one-pager on how we run hosted evals).

Next steps / calendar: If you can drop the sample CSV by EOD Monday (May 17), I’ll schedule a baseline run the following day and share the initial report within 48 hours. If you prefer, we can run the initial job in your dedicated environment (Redwood Dedicated) — that takes a brief setup call.

Questions from today that I promised to follow up on:
- Data retention: by default hosted evals keep logs for 30 days; we can shorten that window or use a private VPC for longer-term tests.
- SOC2 evidence: Marissa (cc’d) will share the SOC2 summary and the security checklist recommended for procurement.

If that plan looks good I’ll send over the HubSpot deal task and a DocuSign quote for an evaluation block (optional).

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop

Hi Sam / Priya — answers inline and a small CSV example below.

1) Scoring rubric (we’ll provide the script and CSV outputs):
- Macro F1 (primary), per-class precision & recall (CSV), and aggregate exact-match for strict labels.
- Human quality score: we surface 1–5 annotations for a 200-row adjudication set; we’ll show correlates with model confidence.
- Regression gates: any drop > 3% absolute on macro F1 or any class with > 5% absolute precision loss triggers a regression alert.

2) Data handling / retention:
- Hosted evals: default logs retained 30 days; we can set retention to 7 days for this run. No raw uploads are shared outside your evaluation instance.
- Redaction: we can run a pre-processing step that replaces commonly sensitive fields with <REDACTED> (SSNs, emails). Mark sensitivity_flag=yes for rows that need redaction.

3) Canary: yes — 200-row canary is perfect. We’ll queue it in a low-cost dev slot, seed stable RNG, and post raw + scored outputs to the Drive folder.

CSV sample (first 3 rows):
id,source_type,raw_text,expected_label,sensitivity_flag,notes
mcy-0001,email,"Patient called to reschedule appointment on 4/10",reschedule,no,"short"
mcy-0002,doc,"Invoice #12345: outstanding balance $250",billing,yes,"contains invoice number"
mcy-0003,webchat,"My prescription was changed; need urgent refill",clinical,no,"triage urgent"

Prompt set (attached sample-prompt-set.md) includes: classification prompt, extraction prompt (for dates/amounts), and a safety filter prompt. We recommend: start with classification temperature=0, max_tokens=128, and use continuous batching with prefix caching for repeated templates.

Recommended models for this workload (initial):
- rwd-13b-v1-q4: higher quality, cost-efficient quantized path (baseline).
- rwd-7b-v2: lower-latency option for production throughput checks.

Operational notes: if you want the run inside your VPC (no uploads to public buckets), we can provision a private evaluation queue — that adds ~2 business days of setup.

I’ve attached: redwood-eval-quickstart.pdf (run instructions), sample-prompt-set.md, and the CSV schema. I’ll also add a HubSpot activity and create the DocuSign eval block quote so finance has the optional pricing.

Thanks — I’ll book the 30-minute setup call once you confirm the canary timing.

Cheers,
Lauren
